cases.title: Slack baseline
cases.proof: All jobs can finish in weeks 1–2 without extra supply or ECLO. Scores are nonnegative, so zero is optimal.

cases.title: ECLO versus deadline slip
cases.proof: Three units require three standard weeks: A incurs 7 days × P2 weight 10 = 70. Two ECLO accesses deliver exactly three units by week 2 for cost 10 in B/C.

cases.title: Five compatible jobs, four sharing places
cases.proof: Only four jobs fit a possession. A delays one job one week (70). B/C buy a second possession at one sector and two platforms: 3 × 7 = 21.

cases.title: PM isolation and PC incompatibility
cases.proof: The three jobs require separate possessions. A completes in weeks 1/2/3: (0+7+14) × 10 = 210. B buys two extra possessions at three locations (42). C permits one extra: two jobs in week 1 and one in week 2 cost 21+70=91.

cases.title: Cross-contract strict precedence
cases.proof: A501 takes weeks 1–2, A502 weeks 3–4, A503 week 5. This meets each deadline with zero cost. Every successor must start in a strictly later week.

cases.title: Live protection through an interchange
cases.proof: Two different opportunities in week 1 deliver both jobs without ECLO or excess. Their mirrored cross-line protection intersects, so assigning the same opportunity must be rejected.

cases.title: Separated demand peaks on one line
cases.proof: A has two one-week P2 delays: 140. B uses ECLO in weeks 1/2 and 4/5 for 20. C can use only one two-week window on X: compress one job for 10 and delay the other for 70. ECLO on just one access cannot remove either delay.

cases.title: Public network with high-priority bottlenecks
cases.oracle: analytical A/C lower bounds; invariant B
cases.proof: Seed 20260918 changes only priority weights and promotes C006/C010 to P1. Feasibility is preserved. The resource-free standard-work A bound is 2240; B's objective is unchanged at 30. C permits at most two ECLO accesses per activity: independently minimizing each activity's delay plus 0/1/2 ECLO costs gives a resource-free lower bound of 720. Valid schedules attain both A/C bounds, proving optimality without relying on CP-SAT's status alone.

cases.title: Two independent copies of the public network
cases.proof: Duplicate every identifier and network resource into two disjoint components. Each feasible solution restricts to a feasible original solution, and two original solutions combine. Scores add, so optima are exactly twice the certified public scores. This is a scale test, not a claim of doubled congestion.

cases.title: Impossible workload within the horizon
cases.proof: One activity needs four units in two weeks. With at most one access per week, even ECLO can deliver only 2 × 1.5 = 3 units. All scenarios must report INFEASIBLE with no partial schedule or export.
